paidTraffic.headlineReady: {{share}} of revenue comes from paid-candidate channels, with about {{profit}} in contribution profit
paidTraffic.headlinePending: There is not enough channel data yet to form a rough paid traffic ROI view
paidTraffic.formula: (Attributed revenue - COGS - payment fees - refund loss - ad spend) / ad spend
paidTraffic.insightReady: {{count}} paid-candidate channels already contribute revenue, so you can start separating profitable channels from channels that only add volume.
paidTraffic.insightPending: Once ad spend is connected, this will move from 'did it drive revenue' to 'did it actually pay back'.

coupon.title: Coupon ROI
coupon.headline: {{cost}} discount cost in the last 30 days, about {{rate}} of revenue
coupon.formula: (Incremental contribution profit from the promotion - coupon cost) / coupon cost
coupon.insight: You already have discount cost and discount-sensitive customer counts ({{discountSensitive}}), which is enough to judge whether promotions are eroding profit, but coupon-code attribution is still missing.
coupon.nextStep: Once coupon code, campaign batch, and promotion type are connected, this can separate high-value discounts from discounts that only buy low-quality orders.

customerValue.title: Customer value
customerValue.headline: {{highValueShare}} high-value customer share and {{score}} average value score
customerValue.formula: Use high-value share, dynamic LTV, at-risk customers, and refund risk to judge whether revenue is coming from customers worth keeping
customerValue.insight: You currently have {{vip}} VIP customers, {{atRisk}} at-risk customers, and {{ltv}} average dynamic LTV, which is enough for a first judgment on whether customer quality is supporting ROI or eroding future value.
customerValue.nextStep: Review changes in high-value and at-risk customer mix first, then decide whether today needs acquisition, activation, or experience repair.

repeat.title: Repeat-purchase ROI
repeat.headline: {{repeatRate}} repeat rate and {{ltv}} average dynamic LTV
repeat.formula: (Incremental contribution profit from repeat purchase - CRM / loyalty / outreach cost) / outreach cost
repeat.insightReady: {{count}} channels already show higher repeat-customer mix, averaging {{share}}, which means repeat behavior is already helping explain long-term ROI.
repeat.insightPending: Customer value is connected, but outreach-cost data is still needed before repeat-purchase ROI can be judged cleanly.
repeat.nextStep: Connect SMS, email, and loyalty costs so this view can tell whether retention work is adding profit or only holding up superficial order counts.

mix.title: Channel scaling ROI
mix.headlineReady: {{top}} looks scalable, while {{low}} should be tightened first
mix.headlinePending: Channel samples are still too thin to rank scaling priorities confidently
mix.formula: Scale channels with stronger contribution profit and limit budget on weak-margin channels
mix.insightReady: The strongest channel contributes about {{topProfit}}, while the weakest-margin channel is only at {{lowMargin}}, which is enough to support a first scale-vs-cut ranking.
mix.insightPending: As channel samples fill in, this will become a steadier guide for who to scale and who to pause.
mix.nextStep: Drill further into products and creatives behind high-profit channels, then review bidding, pages, and discount depth for the weak ones.

adsInsights.trafficPaidSubtitle: Sessions, spend, and payback from ad platforms so you can judge whether media is scaling effective traffic.

adsInsights.trendFreeFootnote: The trend uses GA4 session series to show whether non-paid traffic is growing steadily.
adsInsights.trendSearchFootnote: The trend uses GSC click series so organic search movement is visible on its own.
